cases.description: When the BaseJsonValidator instance has no parent schema assigned (parentSchema == null), getParentSchema() should return null.
After assigning a mock JsonSchema to the protected parentSchema field of a concrete subclass, getParentSchema() must return the same mock instance.
If the parentSchema field is changed after construction (e.g., via reflection or a setter in a subclass), getParentSchema() should reflect the new value and return the updated JsonSchema instance.
A concrete subclass of BaseJsonValidator receives a non‑null parentSchema via its constructor. getParentSchema() must return exactly the instance supplied at construction (identity check).

group: BaseJsonValidator#getParentSchema - reset to null after being set

cases.description: A subclass sets parentSchema to a mock JsonSchema during construction, then later (e.g., via a setter or reflection) resets the field to null. Subsequent call to getParentSchema() should return null.
When parentSchema is non‑null, multiple successive invocations of getParentSchema() must return the exact same object reference each time (no new objects are created).

Assign a custom implementation of JsonSchema (e.g., class CustomJsonSchema extends JsonSchema) to the protected parentSchema field. getParentSchema() should return that subclass instance, confirming polymorphic behavior.

Set parentSchema to a mock JsonSchema whose any method throws a RuntimeException. getParentSchema() must simply return the reference without invoking any method on the mock, therefore no exception should be propagated.
